findings.description: A long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext in the Lambda environment variables block. They are committed to source control, stored in Terraform state, and readable by any principal with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration.

No kms_key_arn is set, so the environment variables holding these secrets are protected only by the default AWS-managed key and are displayed in cleartext in the console/API to anyone with basic Lambda read permissions; no customer-managed key policy constrains decryption.
The function targets the nodejs12.x runtime, which is past end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unremediated.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function executes outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet egress and no security group or subnet-level segmentation, which would ease exfiltration of the embedded credentials if the function code were compromised.

The trust policy allows the whole lambda.amazonaws.com service principal to assume the role with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, so nothing scopes which account or function may obtain the role's credentials.
